reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) is from different alloy systems (AlCrFe2Ni2 and Co-containing NiCrFeCoMn) and does not address Co-free FeNiCrMn. E1 shows strain-rate sensitivity in a different alloy but does not link it to adiabatic shear bands or dislocation mechanisms. E2 reports positive strain-rate sensitivity and deformation bands in a Co-containing alloy but does not establish the specific dislocation/adiabatic shear band mechanism or the temperature-dependent recovery claimed. The key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High strain rates limit thermal activation, causing rapid dislocation nucleation and accumulation
Dislocation accumulation localizes into adiabatic shear bands that dynamically refine microstructure and enhance yield strength
Increasing temperature facilitates thermally activated dislocation mobility and recovery, moderating strain rate sensitivity
Yield strength increases with strain rate at low temperatures due to shear banding and dislocation build-up
At elevated temperatures, yield strength increase with strain rate becomes less pronounced
